## Overview

The between/within split the family gives letter sounds (`lrp-rli-pl-001`), extended to **expressive vocabulary** (#553): pooled across all four waves, how does expressive-vocabulary level go with word-reading level, and does that association live between children or within a child's own movement? The transition counterpart is `lrp-rli-mech-057` (E → W given the period-start word-reading score); this model has no own-baseline term, which is what makes it a levels estimand.

The exposure is split into its child mean and the deviation from it, so the between-child and within-child associations are reported separately rather than blended. The adjustment set mirrors `mech-057` minus the own baseline: hearing, phonological memory and speech production (each with a missing-indicator), the **same-wave standardised logits of taught receptive, taught expressive and receptive vocabulary** as skill adjusters (`gamma_TR`, `gamma_TE`, `gamma_R` — contemporaneous, possibly post-treatment levels, so adjusted associations and the Table-2 fallacy applies), the t1 block-design ability proxy and linear age. Session dose (`attend`) is omitted as in `pl-001`: it is an interval covariate for transitions, not a level. Rows are kept only when the outcome, the exposure and every skill adjuster are observed at the wave; the dropped count is reported.

## Model

$$
\eta = \alpha_{\text{wave}} + \beta_G G
  + \beta_{\text{between}}\bar z_i + \beta_{\text{within}}(z_{it} - \bar z_i)
  + \gamma_A z(A) + \sum_c \gamma_c z(c) + \sum_k \gamma_k z_{k,it} + u_{\text{child}}
$$

where $z_{it}$ is the standardised exposure logit at wave $t$, $\bar z_i$ its
child mean, and $z_{k,it}$ the standardised same-wave logit of skill adjuster $k$
(`TR`, `TE`, `R`). There is deliberately no own-baseline term.
